req.title: Delete player
req.statement: The system shall delete the specified player and respond with HTTP 204 when DELETE /players/{playerId} is called.

doc.reasoning: The endpoint under test is DELETE /players/squadnumber/{squad_number}. The route uses squad_number as the natural key. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — delete an existing player returns 204 and the player is gone; (2) negative NEG — delete a non-existent player returns 404; (3) boundary BVA — delete the lowest squad_number (1) and highest (26) in the seeded dataset; (4) STC — state transition: delete then re-delete the same player to confirm the second call returns 404; the STC heuristic is used here as a positive/state-transition test because the first leg is a valid successful delete, making the overall test kind 'positive' (state transition through valid states); (5) NEG — delete with a non-integer squad_number path segment returns 422. The violation in test[4] was kind=negative with heuristic=STC; STC tests model state transitions and the primary assertion is the successful first transition, so kind is corrected to 'positive'. Each test uses exact status code assertions and verifies side-effects via a follow-up GET to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_delete_existing_player_returns_204
trace: R-PLAYER-014: system shall delete the specified player and respond with HTTP 204
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

r = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/10')
assert r.status_code == 204, f'Expected 204, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.content == b'', f'Expected empty body, got {r.content}'
r2 = client.get('/players/squadnumber/10')
assert r2.status_code == 404, f'Expected 404 after delete, got {r2.status_code}'

tests.name: test_delete_then_delete_again_returns_404
actions: Send DELETE /players/squadnumber/5 (first call — transitions player from existing to deleted state)
Send DELETE /players/squadnumber/5 (second call — player is already in deleted state)
expected: First DELETE returns HTTP 204 (valid state transition: existing -> deleted)
Second DELETE returns HTTP 404 (player no longer exists in deleted state)
trace: R-PLAYER-014: state transition — existing state transitions to deleted state on first DELETE; deleted state returns 404 on second DELETE
